Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — introduces the FeatureLoop benchmark (61 multi-stage tasks with evolution and completion feedback) and compares 12 models under three development workflows (complete requirements upfront, progressive requests, progressive requests with correction)

No SDD approach. Three delegation workflows: Full (complete final specification upfront, one session), Evo (progressive requests, one response per disclosed state), Evo+Comp (progressive requests plus completion feedback, at most two corrective revisions per state). Harness: Claude Code 2.1.74 for all runs. Models: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Kimi K3, Hy4-Preview, DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM 5.3, Qwen 3.8 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash, Grok 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Hy3 (high reasoning where supported, provider-default sampling)

Per task (benchmark side): a behavioural specification per requirement group (actions or inputs, expected outcomes, preserved behaviour, public observation points), a dependency DAG of requirement groups unfolded into stages, user requests written from it, and predefined observations used for feedback. Agents receive only natural-language requests (Full: the complete final specification)

Full: final specification -> one coding session -> final evaluation. Evo: initial request -> response -> check of next state (already satisfied behaviour skipped) -> next request ... -> final evaluation. Evo+Comp: as Evo, plus after each response cumulative checks and up to two completion-feedback messages (generated by Hy4-Preview from up to two predefined observations) before advancing

Tasks: 61 FeatureLoop tasks. Configurations: 12 models x 3 workflows. Baseline: Full workflow (complete requirements upfront) for the workflow comparison; no baseline model. Held constant: harness (Claude Code 2.1.74), 200,000-token context, high reasoning, starting checkpoint, final requirement set and acceptance checks, requirement order (progressive workflows), fixed feedback generator (Hy4-Preview, 20,000-token limit, at most two observations per message), network-disabled environment. Acceptance tests: independently authored executable checks validated across reference states, valid and faulty variants, human review. Repetitions: one run per model-task-workflow. Human intervention: none (automated feedback)

Pooled StrictPass rises from 40.3% (Full) to 51.6% (Evo) and 64.1% (Evo+Comp); repository-clustered 95% intervals [29.9, 50.1], [41.0, 61.5], [53.8, 72.8]. GPT-6 Astra best (72.1% Evo+Comp, FDAC 46.5); Hy3 lowest (36.1%). Only 15.4% (113/733) of observed failed states fully recover within two revisions; 20.9% of successful individual repairs leave another requirement unmet; 11.4% of previously passing requirements later fail. Correction raises mean tokens per run by 47.2%; GLM 5.3 uses about 7.1x Grok 4.6's tokens per successful delivery at similar completion. No significance tests between models; per-model Wilson intervals overlap widely

Distinguished workflows (pooled intervals separate Full from Evo+Comp) and exposed model differences in recovery, retention and token cost that final scores hide; per-model differences mostly within overlapping intervals. Repeatability: not assessed (one run per cell). Limitations stated: one predefined continuation per task, fixed feedback policy, at most two corrective revisions, sampled tasks, check coverage bounded by specified behaviours

Limitations: one predefined continuation per task; fixed feedback policy and two-revision limit; findings tied to sampled tasks and interaction settings; human collaboration may differ; correctness bounded by executable check coverage. Gaps: complete repair, preservation of working behaviour and user-path verification remain obstacles to low-intervention development

Authors (Tencent Hunyuan) evaluate their own Hy3 and Hy4-Preview; Hy4-Preview also generates all completion feedback, and Hy3 was used in candidate screening and benchmark construction (possible bias not discussed). Construction used a routed model pool (Hy3, DeepSeek V4 Flash/Pro, GPT-5.6 Terra/Sol, GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, Claude Opus 5) with Claude Code, Codex and CodeBuddy harnesses. Pooled Evo+Comp StrictPass 469/732 (Table 22) vs 468 successes in the token analysis (telemetry on 731/732 runs, Appendix E.8). Benchmark/data availability Not stated (no link). No pre-registration.
